import re
import pytest
from target import url_basename

def old_url_basename(url):
    m = re.match(r'(?:https?:|)//[^/]+/(?:[^?#]+/)?([^/?#]+)/?(?:[?#]|$)', url)
    if not m:
        return u''
    return m.group(1)

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url",
    [
        # simple paths
        "http://example.com/file",
        "https://example.com/file/",
        "http://example.com/file?query=1",
        "http://example.com/file#fragment",
        "http://example.com/path/file.html",
        "https://example.com/path/to/file/",
        "http://example.com/path/file.html?query=1#frag",
        # root and missing path
        "http://example.com/",
        "http://example.com",
        # scheme-less URL
        "//example.com/file",
        # with port
        "http://example.com:8080/file",
        # with userinfo
        "http://user:pass@example.com/file",
        # multiple segments where old regex allowed slash in the optional part
        "http://example.com/a/b/c",
        "https://example.com/first/second/third",
        # segment containing dot or hidden file
        "http://example.com/.hidden",
        "http://example.com/..",
        # trailing slash after captured segment
        "http://example.com/file/",
        "http://example.com/file/?q=1",
        # query and fragment after captured segment
        "http://example.com/file?x=1",
        "http://example.com/file#section",
        # URLs that should not match (different scheme)
        "ftp://example.com/file",
        "mailto:user@example.com",
        # URL with no double slash after scheme (invalid for pattern)
        "http:/example.com/file",
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_behaviour(url):
    assert url_basename(url) == old_url_basename(url)
